scoring.jobMethod: All-task importance-weighted beta, then percentile (share at or below), rounded to a whole number.
scoring.pathMethod: Equal mean of the distinct direct-route jobs’ rounded, displayed percentiles (required or direct degree routes, direct apprenticeship routes, from the 10 October career dataset); no relevant, progression or candidate routes, no re-ranking. Broader group proxies use the distinct SSC members and are labelled as estimates.
scoring.missingMethod: Exclude missing scores from the mean and disclose partial coverage; never replace missing scores with zero.
scoring.colours: Checker bands: under 40 green, 40–69 amber, 70 and above red.

They protect the wildlife habitat, biodiversity, scenic value, and other unique attributes of preserves and conservation lands. They work in the field and promote awareness and understanding about the natural environment.

tasks.text: Manage wildlife programmes, lakes, or land in assigned areas.
Protect endangered land and marine plants and animals.
Manage wild animal populations through study and conservation practices.
Evaluate and monitor features of nature conservation interest in habitats.
Promote and implement local and national biodiversity action plans in partnership with local and national statutory and voluntary organisations.

exampleCareer.title: Ecologists
exampleCareer.description: Ecologists carry out assessments of the health and distribution of organisms, namely people, plants, and animals, and the relationship between organisms and their environment. Ecologists usually have a specialisation area, such as freshwater, marine, terrestrial, fauna, and flora which they conduct research and perform related tasks.

tasks.text: Conduct research to study ecosystems and environmental changes.
Carry out field surveys to collect data on organism numbers and distribution for databases like the NBN.
Conduct species surveys and inventories.
Analyse data on plants, animals and environmental conditions.
Conduct environmental research to support conservation and sustainability efforts.

exampleCareer.title: Heritage officers
exampleCareer.description: Heritage officers support teams to take care of buildings, monuments and places valued for their cultural and historical importance.

tasks.text: Ensure important buildings, monuments and sites are protected and preserved.
Inspect and survey historic sites and buildings to assess their condition and preservation needs.
Assess the condition of the historic environment.
Plan projects to preserve cultural heritage and historical sites.
Provide advice on conservation, maintenance, and renovation of heritage assets.

exampleCareer.title: Energy managers
exampleCareer.description: Energy managers coordinate the energy use in an organisation and implement policies for increased sustainability, minimisation of cost and environmental impact. They monitor energy use and develop improvement strategies, as well as researching the most beneficial source of energy for the organisation's needs.

tasks.text: Conduct energy audits to evaluate energy use and to identify conservation and cost reduction measures.
Develop strategies to reduce energy consumption.
Identify and prioritise energy-saving measures.
Produce recommendations for enhancing energy performance.
Analyse metered data to track energy consumption and identify trends.

exampleCareer.title: Environmental and geo-environmental engineers
exampleCareer.description: Environmental and geo-environmental engineers research, design, plan, or perform engineering duties in the prevention, control, and repair of environmental hazards using various engineering disciplines. Their work may include waste treatment, site repair, or pollution control technology.

tasks.text: Design systems, processes, or equipment for control, management, or remediation of water, air, or soil quality.
Design safe and sustainable environmental solutions using analysis, modelling, and digital techniques.
Identify risks associated with contaminated land and determine engineering measures to manage those risks with specialists.
Design measures to enhance water and air quality at contaminated sites.
Identify environmental contamination sources.

exampleCareer.title: Environmental consultants
exampleCareer.description: Environmental consultants give advice on environmental matters. They work on areas such as the effects of new developments on the environment, the control of pollution and noise, the effects of agriculture or recreation on plants and wildlife, the effect of climate change and waste management and recycling.

tasks.text: Advise clients on environmental and legal regulations.
Report to and advise clients in consultancy roles.
Interpret and apply regulatory and policy requirements to ensure proposed projects comply with environmental standards.
Advise and collaborate with professionals to address environmental problems.
Advise on actions to reduce environmental risk, based on research and regulatory requirements.

exampleCareer.title: Environmental scientists
exampleCareer.description: Environmental scientists identify problems and find solutions to minimise environmental hazards. They do this by performing analysis on samples such as air, water or soil. They advise on or develop environmental policies that aim to improve water supplies, preservation, and manage waste disposal sites. Environmental scientists perform environmental risk assessments and analyse the environmental impact of new solutions, construction sites or environmental changes ensuring the environmental regulations are followed.

tasks.text: Analyse environmental data.
Collect and analyse pollution samples, such as air or groundwater.
Investigate environmental hazards.
Monitor and assess environmental samples from a range of sources to detect pollutants.
Investigate pollution sources and their environmental effects.

exampleCareer.title: Sustainability officers
exampleCareer.description: Sustainability officers develop programmes for the improvement of environmental sustainability and efficiency within an organisation. They inspect sites to monitor an organisation's compliance with environmental legislation.

tasks.text: Ensure compliance with environmental legislation.
Support the implementation and management of sustainability programmes.
Implement strategies to achieve environmental and sustainability objectives.
Develop plans to meet sustainability targets.
Ensure the implementation of environmental policy and procedures.

exampleCareer.title: Laboratory managers
exampleCareer.description: Laboratory managers oversee the daily operations of a laboratory. They monitor and ensure all laboratory operations are performed according to specifications. They arrange the necessary laboratory equipment and assure that the appropriate health and safety standards are followed.

tasks.text: Manage and oversee laboratory work.
Enforce laboratory safety rules.
Ensure effective lab practices and adherence to Health & Safety procedures.
Organise laboratory work to ensure efficient workflow and accurate results.
Oversee staff to ensure operational efficiency in laboratory operations.

exampleCareer.title: Research and development (R&D) design managers
exampleCareer.description: R&D design managers design and develop manufactured products, such as cars, home appliances and children's toys. They combine artistic talent with research on product use, marketing, and materials to create the most functional and appealing product design.

tasks.text: Design and lead research and development projects.
Direct and coordinate product research and development.
Project manage teams of colleagues involved with the development of new products.
Develop and test concept solutions and alternative designs for products or systems.
Develop new design concepts.

jobs.title: Other natural and social science professionals n.e.c.

exampleCareer.title: Other researchers, unspecified discipline
exampleCareer.description: Other researchers, unspecified discipline perform research activities across a variety of disciplines for academic purposes or to provide the systematic investigation necessary for the development of new products and services, or to enhance the performance of existing ones.

tasks.text: Undertake research to advance knowledge in specific fields.
Carrying out research, often as part of a team.
Conduct research on specific topics.
Conduct research within own field of expertise.
Participate in research projects to advance scientific knowledge.

exampleCareer.title: General practitioners
exampleCareer.description: General practitioners treat all common medical conditions and refer patients to hospitals and other medical services for urgent and specialist treatment. General practitioners do not specialise in any particular area of medicine.

tasks.text: Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Carry out initial consultations on a one-to-one basis with patients to assess their health and get a detailed case history from them.
Diagnose patients' symptoms and refer to specialist consultants if needed.
Examine patients to assess their current condition and health.
Interview patients to obtain their medical histories.

exampleCareer.title: Resident doctors
exampleCareer.description: Resident doctors are fully qualified medical doctors, who diagnose, treat and manage patients under supervision, usually in hospital settings across acute, emergency, medical, and surgical specialties. They provide day-to-day inpatient care, carry out assessments, prescribe within competence, perform procedures appropriate to training level, participate in multidisciplinary care and maintain clinical records.

tasks.text: Assess and examine patients in order to make a diagnosis.
Conduct clinical assessments and diagnose patient conditions.
Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Treat patients in hospital wards or outpatient clinics.
Diagnose and manage clinical presentations collaboratively with patients and colleagues in various care settings.

exampleCareer.title: Anaesthetists
exampleCareer.description: Anaesthetists administer anaesthetics and analgesics for pain management prior to, during, or after surgery.

tasks.text: Manage anaesthesia during surgical procedures to ensure patient safety and comfort.
Monitor anaesthesia to ensure patient safety during procedures.
Maintain life support and airway management for patients.
Administer general anaesthetics to patients to induce unconsciousness for surgery.
Continue anaesthesia in the operating theatre.

exampleCareer.title: Cardiologists
exampleCareer.description: Cardiologists diagnose, treat, manage, and prevent diseases or conditions of the cardiovascular system. They may specialise in interventional procedures.

tasks.text: Diagnose and treat a range of heart-related problems.
Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Conduct clinical assessments and diagnose patient conditions.
Prescribe medication to treat a range of cardiac illnesses.
Design treatment plans based on patient information and medical history.

exampleCareer.title: Dermatologists
exampleCareer.description: Dermatologists diagnose and treat diseases relating to the skin, hair, and nails. They may perform both medical and dermatological surgery functions.

tasks.text: Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Assess and examine patients in order to make a diagnosis.
Recommend specific medical or therapeutic treatments based on patient diagnoses.
Recommend appropriate diagnostic procedures based on patient assessments.
Perform diagnostic tests to identify medical conditions.

exampleCareer.title: Gastroenterologists
exampleCareer.description: Gastroenterologists are doctors who investigate, diagnose, treat and prevent all gastrointestinal (stomach and intestines) and hepatological (liver, gallbladder, biliary tree and pancreas) diseases.

tasks.text: Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Assess and examine patients in order to make a diagnosis.
Recommend specific medical or therapeutic treatments based on patient diagnoses.
Perform diagnostic tests to identify medical conditions.
Monitor and evaluate patient progress to adjust treatment plans.

exampleCareer.title: Gynaecologists and obstetricians
exampleCareer.description: Gynaecologists and obstetricians provide medical care related to pregnancy or childbirth. They diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases of women, particularly those affecting the reproductive system. They may also provide general care to women, as well as perform both medical and gynaecological surgery functions.

tasks.text: Oversee labour progression and delivery during childbirth.
Monitor women during pregnancy.
Provide antenatal care to patients to monitor foetal development and maternal health.
Identify pregnancy-related problems like hypertension, gestational diabetes, pre-term labour, or restricted foetal growth.
Provide antenatal care to patients to support healthy pregnancies.

exampleCareer.title: Haematologists
exampleCareer.description: Haematologists diagnose and clinically manage disorders of the blood and bone marrow. They also provide clinical support for the haematology diagnostic laboratory including the blood bank.

tasks.text: Perform blood tests to diagnose and treat blood disorders.
Provide expert interpretation of test results and guidance on the clinical significance and any follow-up investigations.
Interpret results of diagnostic or laboratory tests.
Make decisions on further haematological analysis and recommend additional tests where appropriate to help with the diagnostic process.
Analyse blood samples using computer-aided and manual techniques.

exampleCareer.title: Homeopaths (medically qualified)
exampleCareer.description: Medically qualified homeopaths treat clients based on the selection and prescription of homeopathic remedies using the homeopathy principle of “like cures like.” Homeopaths in this group require a university degree from a medical school recognised by the General Medical Council. See also 3214/99 - for non-medically qualified Homeopaths.

tasks.text: Determine the optimal use of homeopathic remedies for various conditions.
Plan a course of treatment with patients.
Carry out initial consultations on a one-to-one basis with patients to assess their health and get a detailed case history from them.
Use a holistic approach to advise patients on diet, exercise, lifestyle and emotional wellbeing.
Design a treatment programme based on clients' conditions.

exampleCareer.title: Neurologists
exampleCareer.description: Neurologists diagnose, manage, and treat disorders and diseases of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves, with a primarily nonsurgical focus.

tasks.text: Diagnose complex neurological problems by analysing patient history, conducting examinations, and using neurological tests.
Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Manage neurological disorders to improve patient quality of life.
Assess and examine patients in order to make a diagnosis.
Conduct clinical assessments and diagnose patient conditions.

exampleCareer.title: Oncologists
exampleCareer.description: Oncologists are doctors who diagnose, assess, treat and manage patients with cancers and conduct research that has practical applications.

tasks.text: Develop personalised treatment plans based on patient assessments.
Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Monitor and evaluate patient progress to adjust treatment plans.
Lead or take part in multidisciplinary meetings to support cancer diagnosis and treatment planning.
Recommend specific medical or therapeutic treatments based on patient diagnoses.

exampleCareer.title: Paediatricians
exampleCareer.description: Paediatricians diagnose, treat and help prevent diseases and injuries in children. They may refer patients to specialists for further diagnosis or treatment as needed.

tasks.text: Prescribe or administer treatment and therapy for infants and children.
Assess the condition of children who are ill, injured, or have disabilities.
Treat children with minor illnesses, health problems, and growth concerns.
Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Prescribe medications for children within their care.

exampleCareer.title: Psychiatrists
exampleCareer.description: Psychiatrists diagnose, treat, and seek to prevent mental, emotional, and behavioural disorders through a combination of medical, psychological, and social approaches. They assess patients through interviews, observations, and diagnostic tests, and may prescribe medication, recommend therapeutic interventions, or refer patients to other services.

tasks.text: Administer psychiatric assessments to evaluate mental health conditions.
Identify psychological, emotional, or behavioural issues using information from interviews, tests, records, or reference materials.
Analyse and evaluate patient data or test findings to diagnose the nature or extent of mental disorders.
Assess the risk patients pose to themselves and others.
Have excellent knowledge of physiology, anatomy, psychology, pharmacology and mental health law, as well as an awareness of the social factors that influence mental health.

jobs.title: Medical physicists and nuclear medicine scientists

exampleCareer.title: Radiologists (medically qualified)
exampleCareer.description: Medically qualified radiologists diagnose and treat diseases and injuries using medical imaging techniques, such as x rays, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), nuclear medicine and ultrasounds. They may perform minimally invasive medical procedures and tests.

tasks.text: Use medical imaging to diagnose, treat, and manage various conditions and diseases.
Interpret diagnostic images for patient assessment.
Write up imaging reports.
Perform diagnostic imaging procedures, such as MRI, CT, PET, nuclear cardiology treadmill studies, mammography, and ultrasound.
Review clinical history and previous imaging to inform diagnosis.

exampleCareer.title: Rheumatologists
exampleCareer.description: Rheumatologists diagnose and manage musculoskeletal conditions including inflammatory and non-inflammatory disorders, which can affect people's bones, joints, muscles and soft tissues.

tasks.text: Diagnose patients' medical conditions using records, reports, test results, and examination information.
Monitor and evaluate patient progress to adjust treatment plans.
Recommend specific medical or therapeutic treatments based on patient diagnoses.
Prescribe or administer therapy and medication to treat or prevent illness.
Oversee outpatient clinics to diagnose and manage neurological or rheumatological conditions.

exampleCareer.title: Surgeons
exampleCareer.description: Surgeons perform operations by cutting open a patient's body to repair, remove or replace the diseased or damaged part. They carry out ward rounds and outpatients clinics. They take on a range of administrative duties and teaching responsibilities.

tasks.text: Perform surgeries on patients to repair injuries or treat diseases.
Follow established surgical techniques during the operation.
Determine the need for medical intervention, such as surgery, based on diagnoses.
Monitor patients' progress post-surgery to assess recovery.
Decide on the best care practices for patients before, during, and after surgery.

exampleCareer.title: Physiotherapists
exampleCareer.description: Physiotherapists plan and apply massage, promote and encourage movement and exercise, use hydrotherapy, electro-therapy and other technological equipment in the treatment of a wide range of injuries, diseases and disabilities in order to assist rehabilitation by developing and restoring body systems.

tasks.text: Design and implement exercise therapy programmes for patients.
Prepare programmes of physical treatment to improve patients' physical functioning.
Test joints for ease and range of movement, pain and dysfunction.
Develop personalised treatment plans based on patient assessments.
Apply gentle physiotherapy techniques including stretching, movement, and massage to treat patients.

exampleCareer.title: Occupational therapists
exampleCareer.description: Occupational therapists work with people who have a physical or learning disability or mental illness, actively engaging them in activities in order to maximise self-confidence, independent functioning and well-being.

tasks.text: Teach clients skills for independent living.
Adopt a 'whole person' approach to address each patient's physical and mental wellbeing.
Plan appropriate treatment programmes and interventions in collaboration with colleagues.
Assess patients' physical or psychological needs for tailored activities and techniques.
Monitor and evaluate patient progress to adjust treatment plans.

exampleCareer.title: Speech and language therapists
exampleCareer.description: Speech and language therapists are responsible for the assessment, diagnosis and treatment of speech, language, fluency and voice disorders caused by disability, injury or illness.

tasks.text: Identify the speech and communication difficulty or disorder.
Design a treatment programme based on clients' conditions.
Assess the cause and nature of problems, including congenital issues like cleft palate or acquired disorders.
Monitor and evaluate patient progress to adjust treatment plans.
Develop speech exercise programmes to reduce disabilities.

exampleCareer.title: Cognitive behavioural therapists
exampleCareer.description: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) therapists use talking therapy to challenge negative patterns of thought to help patients change unwanted patterns of thinking or behaviour.

tasks.text: Provide evidence-based individual therapy, such as cognitive behaviour therapy for depression and anxiety.
Assess if a client will benefit from cognitive behavioural therapy.
Establish and maintain trust with patients to support their treatment.
Assess clients' needs to create personalised therapy sessions.
Encourage the client to talk about and explore their feelings, attitudes and behaviours.

exampleCareer.title: Psychotherapists
exampleCareer.description: Psychotherapists treat clients with varying degrees of psychological, psychosocial, or psychosomatic behavioural disorders and pathogenic conditions. They use a range of psychotherapeutic methods to promote personal development and wellbeing and provide advice on improving relationships, capabilities and problem-solving techniques.

tasks.text: Conduct individual psychotherapy for those with chronic or acute mental health conditions.
Encourage the client to talk about and explore their feelings, attitudes and behaviours.
Engage with clients to understand their needs and requirements.
Offer therapy and treatments for issues relating to a range of mental health conditions.
Deliver therapy sessions with a variety of clients individually or in groups.

exampleCareer.title: Clinical psychologists
exampleCareer.description: Clinical psychologists work with people experiencing emotional, psychological or behavioural distress, perform tests and assess their emotional, cognitive and behavioural processes, and determine treatments to help patients improve their mental wellbeing.

tasks.text: Conduct psychological assessment to identify the priorities and requirements for personalised, evidence-based psychological interventions.
Assess clients' needs and abilities using psychometric tests, interviews, and direct observation.
Develop psychological formulations to inform personalised care and enhance psychological interventions for professional use.
Identify psychological, emotional, or behavioural issues using information from interviews, tests, records, or reference materials.
Evaluate patients' behaviour to formulate diagnoses or assess treatments.

exampleCareer.title: Counselling psychologists
exampleCareer.description: Counselling psychologists use psychological theory and research in therapeutic work to help clients with a range of difficult life issues and/or mental health conditions. Clients can include children, adults, families, couples and groups.

tasks.text: Build a relationship of trust and respect with clients.
Encourage the client to talk about and explore their feelings, attitudes and behaviours.
Offer counselling services tailored to individual needs.
Deliver therapy sessions with a variety of clients individually or in groups.
Support clients in finding ways to manage their issues and make positive changes.

exampleCareer.title: Educational psychologists
exampleCareer.description: Educational psychologists are psychologists employed by educational institutions to provide psychological and emotional support to students in need. They are specialised in the provision of direct support and interventions to students, conducting psychological testing and assessment. They also consult with families, teachers and other school-based student support professionals, such as school social workers and educational counsellors, about the students. They may also work with the school administration to improve practical support strategies to improve the students' wellbeing.

tasks.text: Administer standardised ability and achievement tests, and interpret results to determine students' strengths and needs.
Identify and develop intervention strategies, tutoring plans, or individualised education plans (IEPs) for students.
Assess children with learning difficulties.
Support parents, teachers and others involved with the education of children and young people.
Develop individual education plans (IEPs) designed to promote pupils' educational, physical, or social development.

exampleCareer.title: Forensic psychologists
exampleCareer.description: Forensic psychologists apply psychological theory to criminal investigation to help understand psychological problems associated with criminal behaviour and the treatment of those who have committed offences.

tasks.text: Perform risk assessments on offenders.

Carry out risk assessments on service users who pose higher levels of risk with complex needs, including sex offenders, domestic abuse perpetrators, individuals who resort to violence and extremist activities.
Prepare written evaluations of individuals' psychological competence for court hearings.
Develop offender treatment and rehabilitation programmes.
Write client reports on psychological assessments.

exampleCareer.title: Occupational psychologists
exampleCareer.description: Occupational psychologists focus on how people behave at work to increase their productivity, job satisfaction and the overall effectiveness of an organisation.

tasks.text: Analyse job requirements to establish criteria for classification and selection.
Advise management on personnel policies to enhance organisational effectiveness.
Identify training and development needs within an organisation through job analysis, appraisal schemes and regular consultation with business managers and HR departments.
Develop employee selection programmes.
Study organisational effectiveness, productivity, and efficiency, including the nature of workplace supervision and leadership.

exampleCareer.title: Acupuncturists
exampleCareer.description: Acupuncturists make use of thin needles and insert them into acupuncture points in the body to restore the imbalances of the human body and overall good health.

tasks.text: Insert needles to provide acupuncture treatment.
Identify correct anatomical points for treatments based on patient's anatomy and treatment precautions.
Carry out infection control procedures.
Provide treatment to patients following their assessment.
Carry out initial consultations on a one-to-one basis with patients to assess their health and get a detailed case history from them.

exampleCareer.title: Art therapists
exampleCareer.description: Art therapists help patients overcome psychological and emotional difficulties and facilitate self-understanding through an artistic process which reflects emotions and feelings.

tasks.text: Conduct art therapy sessions, providing guided self-expression experiences to help clients recover from, or cope with, cognitive, emotional, or physical impairments.
Communicate through art and shared experiences to support client wellbeing and facilitate positive behavioural and communicative changes.
Enable clients to explore their artwork and the process they used to create it.
Design art therapy sessions or programmes to meet client's goals or objectives.
Assist clients in expressing their feelings.

exampleCareer.title: Chiropractors and osteopaths
exampleCareer.description: Chiropractors and osteopaths use their hands to help relieve problems with the musculoskeletal system. They mainly use manipulation of the body tissues, touch, stretching and massage techniques to relieve the patients' pain and promote a healthy lifestyle. Chiropractors primarily focus on the spine, joints and the muscles, whilst osteopaths are also concerned with the rest of the body.

tasks.text: Carry out manipulations of the joints of the spine and extremities using hands or specialist equipment.
Assess the functioning of the neuromusculoskeletal system and the spine using chiropractic diagnostic methods.
Test joints for ease and range of movement, pain and dysfunction.
Reduce pain using manual therapy methods.
Assess and examine patients in order to make a diagnosis.

exampleCareer.title: Drama therapists
exampleCareer.description: Drama therapists use role play, voice work, movement and storytelling to help clients explore and solve personal and social problems.

tasks.text: Support clients in creative drama and theatre work using improvisation and storytelling techniques.
Ensure a safe and secure therapeutic environment while working creatively with various client groups.
Facilitate safe expression and role-play of emotions and situations for clients.
Establish and maintain a safe practice environment, maintaining confidentiality and records appropriately.
Practise within the profession's legal and ethical boundaries.

exampleCareer.title: Music therapists
exampleCareer.description: Music therapists use music creatively to help their clients address social, emotional or physical difficulties.

tasks.text: Use a variety of musical styles and instruments in client-led, group or individual therapy sessions.
Take an active role in sessions by playing, singing and listening.
Ensure a safe and secure therapeutic environment while working creatively with various client groups.
Deliver therapy sessions with a variety of clients individually or in groups.
Design music therapy experiences to address client needs.

exampleCareer.title: Nutritionists
exampleCareer.description: Nutritionists use food science knowledge to help individuals and groups make the right choices about what they eat. They often work within community settings or local authority public health teams, focusing primarily on health promotion. They work directly with acutely ill or hospitalised patients under the supervision of either a dietitian or other suitable, regulated, health professional.

tasks.text: Advise clients on nutrition and lifestyle changes for improved health.
Provide dietary advice to promote healthy eating habits.
Offer guidance on dietary and lifestyle choices to promote optimal health.
Provide scientific advice on healthy eating.
Consult with clients about their health, diet, and lifestyle.

exampleCareer.title: Orthoptists
exampleCareer.description: Orthoptists diagnose and treat eye movement disorders, as well as visual impairments related to the way the eyes interact with the brain. They will spot serious neurological conditions, such as multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease. They work with adults children and babies.

tasks.text: Diagnose eye position and movement disorders.
Diagnose disorders of the visual system with an emphasis on binocular vision or abnormal eye movements.
Diagnose squints, amblyopia, reduced or double vision, and disorders.
Conduct orthoptic motor testing to diagnose visual issues.
Formulate a treatment plan, which might include prescribing an eye patch, eye exercises or the use of prisms.

exampleCareer.title: Play therapists
exampleCareer.description: Play therapists use play as a communication tool to help children understand their world and deal with emotional distress and trauma.

tasks.text: Establish a safe environment for children to use play as a means of expression and coping with their issues.
Ensure a safe and secure therapeutic environment while working creatively with various client groups.
Build meaningful therapeutic relationships with children and young people through effective communication.
Develop playful yet professional relationships with children.
Provide a safe environment for children.

exampleCareer.title: Psychological wellbeing practitioners
exampleCareer.description: Psychological wellbeing practitioners assess and support adults who are experiencing common mental health difficulties such as mild to moderate symptoms of depression, anxiety and low mood.

tasks.text: Provide low-intensity interventions, such as psycho-educational interventions, guided self-help and computerised CBT.
Conduct psychological assessment to identify the priorities and requirements for personalised, evidence-based psychological interventions.

Deliver within a stepped care service delivery model , to treat patients at the lowest appropriate level in the first instance, only 'stepping up' to intensive/specialist services as clinically required.
Handle personal, confidential, and sensitive information with strict adherence to legal and organisational confidentiality policies.
Make decisions on the suitability of new referrals, referring clients to alternative services or 'stepping up' their treatment to high-intensity psychological therapy if necessary.

exampleCareer.title: Sports therapists
exampleCareer.description: Sports therapists use their knowledge and skills to treat sporting injuries, advise on injury prevention and support rehabilitation, using a range of physical techniques and therapies.

tasks.text: Evaluate and treat athletes' injuries for rehabilitation.
Assess athletes' injuries to develop recovery plans.
Perform a range of prehab and rehabilitation procedures, including recovery protocols to maintain high levels of repeated physical performance daily, and throughout the year.
Design and implement exercise therapy programmes for patients.
Test joints for ease and range of movement, pain and dysfunction.

exampleCareer.title: Midwifery nurses
exampleCareer.description: Midwifery nurses deliver, or assist in the delivery of babies, provide antenatal and postnatal care and advise parents on baby care. They work with other healthcare professionals and advise on and teach midwifery practice.

tasks.text: Assist in the delivery of babies.
Oversee labour progression and delivery during childbirth.
Provide antenatal care to patients to support healthy pregnancies.
Provide antenatal care to patients to monitor foetal development and maternal health.
Provide postnatal care to patients.

exampleCareer.title: Learning disability community nurses
exampleCareer.description: Learning disability community nurses work in community settings to help people with learning disabilities maintain their health and wellbeing and to live their lives as fully and independently as possible. They draw up care plans and monitor the implementation of recommendations. They provide care in the community outside of a hospital environment.

tasks.text: Work with adults with health and social care needs or learning disabilities.
Assist individuals with learning disabilities in accessing healthcare services and overcoming related challenges.
Put patients at the centre of care.
Write care plans.
Communicate with a range of patients using easily understood language.

exampleCareer.title: General practice nurses
exampleCareer.description: General practice nurses provide a wide range of patient care in a GP surgery, including administering vaccinations, managing long-term conditions like diabetes and asthma, performing wound care, and conducting health screenings and advice. They work as part of a primary healthcare team alongside GPs and other professionals to deliver treatment, education, and health promotion for patients.

tasks.text: Manage long-term conditions to provide continuity of care for patients with chronic illness.
Offer services to assist patients in managing conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
Organise and provide vaccinations, such as the flu jab.
Provide ongoing support and advice to patients under long-term care.
Provide patients with advice and counselling on health promotion and disease prevention.

exampleCareer.title: Diabetes specialist nurses
exampleCareer.description: Diabetes specialist nurses provide good patient care and promote self-care management. They work wholly in diabetes care and may be employed in a variety of care settings.

tasks.text: Teach diabetes management techniques for independent living.
Provide guidance to patients on managing chronic health conditions.
Provide ongoing support and advice to patients under long-term care.
Educate patients and their carers about how to prevent and/or improve conditions.
Support, advise and educate patients and close relatives.

exampleCareer.title: Intensive care nurses
exampleCareer.description: Intensive care nurses are specialist registered nurses who provide constant monitoring and care for patients in a seriously ill or unstable condition.

tasks.text: Maintain life support and airway management for patients.
Monitor symptoms or changes in patients' conditions.
Monitor patients' physiological responses using invasive and noninvasive techniques.
Respond to emergency situations by providing airway management, administering emergency fluids or drugs, or using basic or advanced cardiac life support techniques.
Prioritise nursing care for assigned critically ill patients, based on assessment data or identified needs.

exampleCareer.title: Theatre nurses
exampleCareer.description: Theatre nurses are specialist registered nurses who work in hospital operating theatres and anaesthetic/recovery areas with patients in each phase of a person's operation.

tasks.text: Prepare the operating theatre and make sure drugs and specialist equipment are available.
Inspect instruments, equipment, and operating theatres to ensure sterility.
Conduct safety checks in operating theatres to ensure compliance with medical safety standards.
Gather surgical instruments and supplies for theatre procedures.
Ensure operating theatres are tidy and prepared for procedures.

exampleCareer.title: Infection prevention and control nurses
exampleCareer.description: Infection prevention and control nurses (IPC) work to stop the spread of infections in healthcare and community settings by creating and implementing policies, educating staff and the public, and monitoring for outbreaks. Their duties include developing infection control procedures, investigating outbreaks, ensuring compliance with hand hygiene and sanitation standards, and providing expert advice on preventing the transmission of micro-organisms.

tasks.text: Direct activities for stopping the spread of infections in facilities.
Implement measures to prevent the spread of infectious diseases.
Investigate outbreaks of infectious disease.
Monitor and report incidents of infectious diseases to local and national health agencies.
Maintain departmental policies, procedures, objectives, and infection control standards.

exampleCareer.title: Palliative care specialist nurses
exampleCareer.description: Palliative care specialist nurses provide specialist nursing and care for people who are living with terminal illnesses, and support families through difficult times. They manage complex symptoms, coordinate care across settings, advance care planning and end‑of‑life care.

tasks.text: Communicate complex sensitive information effectively with individuals, their families, carers and health and care professionals.
Provide emotional support for patients and their families.
Inform clients about end-of-life symptoms and options to assist them in making informed decisions.
Provide support and reassurance to patients, taking into account their physical and psychological needs.
Provide support to clients, their families, and carers.

jobs.title: Mental health and healthcare social workers

exampleCareer.title: Mental health nurse practitioners
exampleCareer.description: Mental health nurse practitioners are trained specialist nurses who work with individuals, families, groups, and communities. They assess mental health needs and develop a nursing diagnosis and plan of care. They undertake additional medical education to provide advanced nursing care, assess and diagnose patients, prescribe medication and refer patients to hospital doctors if required.

tasks.text: Assess the physical and mental health needs of individuals.
Administer psychiatric assessments to evaluate mental health conditions.
Provide nursing care to individuals with mental health conditions or emotional disturbances.
Conduct clinical assessments and diagnose patient conditions.
Provide direct care to patients with mental health conditions to maintain safe, high-quality practice.

exampleCareer.title: Other registered nurse practitioners
exampleCareer.description: Other registered nurse practitioners provide advanced nursing care for individuals who are sick, injured or otherwise in need of clinical support. They work independently and alongside medical doctors and other healthcare professionals, managing their own caseload while contributing to emergency and planned care. Their responsibilities include assessing and diagnosing patients, ordering and interpreting diagnostic tests, determining treatment plans and prescribing medication. They monitor patients progress, administer medicines and treatments, apply surgical dressings, and deliver other forms of treatment. This group excludes occupations categorised under sub-unit groups: 2234/01 - Mental health nurse practitioners.

tasks.text: Plan, deliver, monitor, and evaluate complex care independently using enhanced clinical assessments, diagnostics, and interventions.
Conduct clinical assessments and diagnose patient conditions.
Prescribe necessary medication based on patient assessments.
Prescribe medications to treat various health conditions.
Provide care and clinical support to individuals of all ages within an agreed scope of practice.

jobs.title: Mental health and healthcare social workers

exampleCareer.title: Registered mental health nurses
exampleCareer.description: Registered mental health nurses support and care for people with a range of mental health conditions, in hospital and community settings, and help them towards recovery and management of their conditions.

tasks.text: Provide nursing care to individuals with mental health conditions or emotional disturbances.
Establish and maintain trust with patients to support their treatment.
Provide direct care to patients with mental health conditions to maintain safe, high-quality practice.
Communicate complex sensitive information effectively with individuals, their families, carers and health and care professionals.
Provide support and reassurance to patients, taking into account their physical and psychological needs.

exampleCareer.title: Neonatal nurses
exampleCareer.description: Neonatal nurses care for newborn babies who are born premature or sick. They provide 24 hour care in acute hospitals and work shifts in intensive care, high dependency and special care baby units. Some nurses work in the community, providing continuing care and support for babies and their families who have been recently discharged from hospital.

tasks.text: Monitor symptoms or changes in patients' conditions.
Provide safe and compassionate nursing care that puts people's best interests first.
Prioritise nursing care for assigned critically ill patients, based on assessment data or identified needs.
Administer medications to infants and children.
Log patients' medical information and vital signs.

exampleCareer.title: Paediatric nurses
exampleCareer.description: Paediatric nurses assess the nursing needs of children of all ages who are suffering from many different illnesses and conditions.

tasks.text: Assess the condition of children who are ill, injured, or have disabilities.
Assess patients through observation and interviews to identify care needs.
Assess each child's needs in consultation with professionals and parents.
Identify patients' age-specific needs and alter care plans as necessary to meet those needs.
Assess patients to evaluate their health condition.

exampleCareer.title: School nurses
exampleCareer.description: School nurses are qualified and registered nurses who work across education and health, providing a link between school, home and the community. Their aim is to improve the health and wellbeing of children and young people. They work with families and young people from five to nineteen and are usually linked to a school or group of schools.

tasks.text: Provide safe and compassionate nursing care that puts people's best interests first.
Work collaboratively with other professionals and teams to promote and protect the health and wellbeing of individuals, groups and communities.
Collaborate with healthcare and educational professionals to provide holistic client care.
Assess the needs of young people in areas such as health and relationships.
Provide professional care with accountability and autonomy in partnership with service users.

exampleCareer.title: Other registered nursing professionals
exampleCareer.description: Other registered nursing professionals provide general nursing care for the sick, injured and others in need of such care, assist medical doctors with their tasks and work with other healthcare professionals and within teams of healthcare workers in a variety of other professional nursing occupations not elsewhere classified in MINOR GROUP 223: Nursing Professionals.

tasks.text: Provide evidence-based nursing care.
Provide nursing care to individuals and groups.
Conduct comprehensive holistic assessments of patients to determine their care needs.
Assess patients through observation and interviews to identify care needs.
Provide professional care with accountability and autonomy in partnership with service users.

exampleCareer.title: Veterinarians
exampleCareer.description: Veterinarians diagnose and treat animal injuries, diseases and disorders, and advise on preventative action. They may work in practices, specialising according to their location in either a rural or urban area, or in the public sector or associated industries such as pharmaceuticals, food production or drug regulation.

tasks.text: Diagnose and treat sick and injured animals.
Examine animals to detect symptoms of illness or injury.
Complete physical checks on animals to assess health and diagnose conditions.
Monitor animal health and welfare.
Recommend medicines, vaccinations, and specialised medical care for disease or injury.

exampleCareer.title: Pharmacists
exampleCareer.description: Pharmacists dispense drugs and medicaments in hospitals and pharmacies and advise on and participate in the development and testing of new drugs, compounds and therapies. They counsel on the proper use and adverse effects of drugs and medicines.

exampleCareer.title: Optometrists
exampleCareer.description: Optometrists test patients' vision, diagnose defects and disorders and prescribe glasses or contact lenses as required.

exampleCareer.title: Dentists and dental surgeons
exampleCareer.description: Dentists and dental surgeons prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues. Dental surgeons treat wisdom teeth, perform complex extractions and correct congenital growth defects.

exampleCareer.description: Orthodontists examine, diagnose and treat dental malocclusions (crooked teeth) and oral cavity anomalies. They design and fabricate appliances to realign teeth and jaws to produce and maintain normal function and to improve appearance.

Apply dental appliances as per treatment plans.

exampleCareer.title: Diagnostic radiographers
exampleCareer.description: Diagnostic radiographers operate imaging equipment to produce high-quality images of the body for the diagnosis and monitoring of injury and disease. They work across a range of imaging modalities including X-ray, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ultrasound, and fluoroscopy. Responsibilities include preparing and positioning patients, ensuring radiation protection protocols are followed, interpreting images to inform clinical decisions, and maintaining imaging equipment.

exampleCareer.description: Therapeutic radiographers prepare and perform safe and accurate high-energy radiation treatments to patients, using a wide range of sophisticated equipment and techniques, to target the area to be treated. Follow policies and procedures for radiation workers to ensure personnel safety.

exampleCareer.title: Sonographers
exampleCareer.description: Sonographers perform diagnostic ultrasound examinations using ultrasonic imaging devices to produce images for the assessment, diagnosis and monitoring of medical conditions, and provide clinical reports to referring practitioners. Practitioners may work at advanced or consultant level, undertaking complex cases.

exampleCareer.description: Paramedics provide first aid and life support treatment in emergency situations and transport sick and injured people who require skilled treatment.

exampleCareer.title: Podiatrists
exampleCareer.description: Podiatrists (formerly known as chiropodists) diagnose and treat ailments and abnormalities of the human foot and lower limb, deal with minor infections, injuries and deformities, and conditions resulting from other major health disorders such as diabetes. exampleCareer.title: Audiologists
exampleCareer.description: Audiologists assess, diagnose and treat patients with audiological and vestibular disorders caused by infectious, genetic, traumatic or degenerative conditions, such as hearing loss, tinnitus, dizziness, imbalance, hyperacusis and auditory processing difficulties. exampleCareer.description: Cardiac physiologists analyse known and suspected heart disease. exampleCareer.description: Dietitians assess specific nutritional requirements of populations or individuals throughout their lives and translate this into advice which will maintain, reduce risk to, or restore people's health. Locate, handle, store, load, transport and position materials and tools safely, minimising damage and complying with health and safety regulations.
Load and unload goods from lorries for delivery and transport operations.
Store items in an orderly and accessible manner in warehouses, tool rooms, stores, or other areas.
Unload incoming shipments into designated storage areas.

exampleCareer.title: Delivery operatives
exampleCareer.description: Delivery operatives load and unload goods from removal vans and delivery vehicles, convey household and office furniture, goods, equipment or other items, accompany drivers of road vehicles, and perform other elementary goods handling tasks.

tasks.text: Load and unload cargo from vehicles to ensure safe and efficient transport.
Unload items at the destination.
Load and unload goods from lorries for delivery and transport operations.
Locate, handle, store, load, transport and position materials and tools safely, minimising damage and complying with health and safety regulations.
Move heavy furniture, equipment, or supplies, either manually or with sack barrows.

exampleCareer.title: Dockers, slingers and stevedores
exampleCareer.description: Dockers, slingers and stevedores work in ports and are involved in the loading and unloading of goods onto ships.

tasks.text: Load and unload cargo from vessels to facilitate maritime transport.
Operate ship loading and unloading equipment.
Operate heavy machinery and lifting equipment to handle cargo and materials.
Assist in loading and unloading goods safely.
Secure and maintain the integrity of cargo during transportation.

exampleCareer.title: Bar and catering supervisors
exampleCareer.description: Bar and catering supervisors oversee operations and directly supervise and coordinate the activities of those working in the catering industry, in bars, restaurants and other establishments.

tasks.text: Supervise catering staff.
Manage staff to ensure efficient operation of the establishment.
Supervise other bar staff during service.
Ensure each stage of food and beverage service meets business/brand standard, including customer arrival, provision of information, taking orders, serving food and drink, and taking payments.
Coordinate an effective bar service, ensuring licensing laws are adhered to at all times, customer issues are dealt with and potential conflict minimised.

exampleCareer.title: Hospital porters
exampleCareer.description: Hospital porters perform various manual tasks in hospitals to assist nursing and domestic staff with the care of patients.

tasks.text: Move patients on trolleys or in wheelchairs between wards and departments.
Transport patients to the hospital or within the hospital.
Transport patients to and from treatment areas, using wheelchairs or providing standing support.
Transport specimens, laboratory items, or pharmacy items, ensuring proper documentation and delivery to authorised personnel.
Place patients on trolleys with assistance from other attendants.

exampleCareer.title: Kitchen and catering assistants
exampleCareer.description: Kitchen and catering assistants assist in the preparation and service of food and beverages in restaurants, cafés and other eating establishments, and perform various cleaning, fetching and carrying tasks.

tasks.text: Follow food hygiene regulations.
Handle raw food according to food hygiene standards.
Clean or sanitise work areas, utensils, or equipment.
Maintain kitchen work areas, equipment, and utensils in clean condition.
Monitor and record food temperatures to ensure food safety.

exampleCareer.title: Waiters and waitresses
exampleCareer.description: Waiters and waitresses serve food and beverages in hotels, clubs, restaurants public houses and other establishments. See also 6219/02 - Ship stewards (excludes catering).

tasks.text: Provide excellent customer service by understanding the needs and expectations of customers.
Serve customers to ensure their satisfaction with products and services.
Serve food and drinks to guests.
Take food and drink orders from customers.
Serve customers at tables or counters.

exampleCareer.title: Bar staff
exampleCareer.description: Bar staff prepare, mix and serve alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks and beverages at bars in public houses, hotels, clubs and other establishments.

tasks.text: Serve clients with beverages and manage the premises.
Provide excellent customer service by understanding the needs and expectations of customers.
Mix and prepare flavours for mixed drinks.
Serve beverages that meet guest expectations and business standards.
Verify customers' identification to ensure age requirements for alcohol purchase are met.

exampleCareer.title: Coffee shop workers
exampleCareer.description: Coffee shop workers make and serve coffee, food and other beverages in coffee shops and cafés, and perform various cleaning, fetching and carrying tasks.

tasks.text: Prepare and serve beverages, such as coffee or soft drinks.
Provide excellent customer service by understanding the needs and expectations of customers.
Brew coffee and tea for guests.
Take customer orders to provide personalised service.
Communicate with customers to address their needs.

exampleCareer.title: Arcade attendants
exampleCareer.description: Arcade attendants supervise and maintain amusement arcade machines and facilities, assist customers with gameplay or machine issues, handle token or credit systems, and ensure cleanliness and safety within the premises.

tasks.text: Perform minor repairs or make adjustments to fruit machines, resolving problems such as machine tilts and coin jams.
Maintain venue cleanliness and security to comply with health and safety regulations.
Maintain familiarity with the games at a facility.
Explain fruit machine functions and payouts to customers upon inquiry.
Check machinery for wear and damage.

exampleCareer.title: Cinema and theatre attendants
exampleCareer.description: Cinema and theatre attendants, also known as ushers, work in the foyer and auditorium of a cinema or theatre. They sell tickets and refreshments, control public access, show people to their seats and undertake cleaning duties.

tasks.text: Check tickets and other relevant documents for an event.
Provide excellent customer service, responding to inquiries and addressing any concerns or issues.
Inspect tickets and passes for validity.
Show people to their seats.
Collect admission tickets, passes, or facility memberships from patrons at entertainment events.

exampleCareer.title: Event stewards
exampleCareer.description: Event stewards greet, assist and direct people attending events. They may check tickets, search people attending events to ensure that no prohibited or restricted items are taken into venues and ensure the safety of people attending events.

tasks.text: Screen individuals and belongings to prevent passage of prohibited materials using walkthrough detectors, wands, or bag searches.
Maintain order during public meetings, social events, and processions.
Move among visitors, patrons, or employees to maintain order and protect property.
Monitor and enforce compliance with safety rules and regulations in a workplace.
Guide patrons to exits or provide other instructions or assistance in case of emergency.

exampleCareer.title: Gallery and museum attendants
exampleCareer.description: Gallery and museum attendants greet visitors, attend to enquiries and ensure the protection of exhibits.

tasks.text: Greet and assist visitors with information about exhibits.
Provide relevant information to visitors.
Serve customers by handling enquiries and providing appropriate support during their visit.
Move among visitors, patrons, or employees to maintain order and protect property.
Answer routine enquiries from patrons.

exampleCareer.title: Ride attendants
exampleCareer.description: Ride attendants operate rides at theme parks and fairgrounds. They may collect tickets or explain safety procedures to riders.

tasks.text: Operate mechanical riding devices in amusement parks, funfairs, or recreation areas.
Explain and enforce safety rules and regulations.
Fasten safety devices for patrons at rides and events.
Assist passengers with safe boarding and alighting from the vehicle.
Enforce rules and regulations of recreational facilities to maintain discipline and ensure safety.

exampleCareer.title: Bingo callers and assistants
exampleCareer.description: Bingo callers and assistants organise and run games of bingo in a bingo hall, social club or other entertainment facility.

tasks.text: Announce winning numbers or colours during games.
Ensure game operations follow house rules and regulations.
Start gaming equipment that randomly selects numbered balls.
Pay out winnings or direct customers to gaming cashiers for collection.
Calculate and verify amounts won or lost in gaming activities.

exampleCareer.title: Clairvoyants, mediums and astrologers
exampleCareer.description: Clairvoyants, mediums and astrologers claim to have extra-sensory talents enabling them to act as communicators between the natural/spiritual world. They offer advice to clients about topics such as health, money and love. They may use methods such as tarot card reading, palm reading or use astrological charts.

tasks.text: Assess the needs of clients by listening and providing guidance.
Serve clients by providing spiritual guidance and support.
Foster a safe and nurturing environment for clients to express their concerns.
Advise individuals on their spiritual needs for personal development.
Assess and understand clients' feelings or temperament.

exampleCareer.title: Stagehands
exampleCareer.description: Stagehands assist stage technicians setting up and preparing equipment for live performance. Their work includes setting up the scenery, lights, sound, props, rigging and special effects for a production.

tasks.text: Rig stage equipment and perform safety checks before events.
Set up and dismantle the performance area at theatres.
Attach loads to rigging to provide support or prepare them for moving, using hand and power tools.
Erect rigging or hoisting equipment to support lighting installations.
Oversee the stage area to ensure it is ready for performances.

exampleCareer.title: Hotel porters
exampleCareer.description: Hotel porters assist guests with luggage, escort them to rooms, and provide general support within hotel premises. They may also handle deliveries, run errands, and respond to guest requests to ensure a smooth and welcoming experience. Duties are typically performed in hotels, resorts, and similar accommodation establishments.

tasks.text: Transport luggage between assigned rooms, terminals, or platforms.
Address guests' requests to ensure a pleasant stay.
Escort guests to their rooms.
Meet and greet customers upon arrival at the hotel.
Serve customers by handling enquiries and providing appropriate support during their visit.

exampleCareer.title: Clinical trials coordinators
exampleCareer.description: Clinical trials coordinators supervise drug trials and medical research. They recruit and screen patients who fit the guidelines of the trial and source the necessary materials and supplies for the trials. Coordinators are responsible for ensuring the trial meets all regulations including those regarding safety, government rules and regulations as well as company or hospital ethics.

tasks.text: Apply good clinical practice (GCP) regulations and corporate ethics to ensure patients' rights, safety, and well-being are not compromised during clinical trials.
Oversee participant enrolment, ensuring informed consent is obtained and documented.
Monitor compliance with regulations in clinical research projects.
Screen potential subjects to determine their suitability as study participants.
Maintain Trial Master Files (TMFs) and ensure confidentiality and traceability of documentation in clinical trials.

Record finds and sites using photography, detailed notes and drawings.
Describe the materials, size, shape, function, and decoration of artefacts.
Make independent and authoritative identifications of archaeological materials or data in a specialist area, by applying advanced knowledge and understanding.
